sections.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains that the reason each world contains all three categories of Chabad, Chagat, and Nehi is to account for the thirty vessels, and this inter-inclusion parallels the inter-inclusion of the four categories of inanimate, vegetative, animate, and human, which relates to Divine Providence from the level of the essential concealment of the Awtsmoos.

translations.translation: Now, what is relevant in the maamar to explain that in each world there are the three categories of Chabad, Chagat, and Nehi
(simply)
is,
because otherwise the matter of the number of thirty vessels is not understood.
For ostensibly,
since in Beriah only the aspect of Chabad of the vessels of Atzilus is drawn down,
in Yetzirah only the aspect of Chagat,
and in Asiyah only the aspect of Nehi,
then there are only three times three,
and what is the matter of thirty vessels?
Therefore he explains,
that in each world there are all three categories, etc.
However, more deeply,
this matter—that in each world there are all the categories—
relates to the entire content of the maamar.
For,
that in the world of Beriah there are also Chagat and Nehi,
and likewise the aspect of Chabad and Nehi in Yetzirah,
Chabad and Chagat in Asiyah,
is analogous to the inter-inclusion of the inanimate, vegetative, animate, and human that is explained in the maamar below,
that the change and distinction between the four types of inanimate, vegetative, animate, and human is only from the aspect of revelation,
but from the aspect of concealment,
they are all equal.
And based on this he explains
the matter of particular Divine Providence in all parts of the inanimate, vegetative, animate, and human of Asiyah
[and likewise in the four worlds Atzilus, Beriah, Yetzirah, Asiyah, which are likened to inanimate, vegetative, animate, and human],
for the Providence from the aspect of the Essence of Ein Sof, which is in the aspect of concealment,
is equal in all of them.
That is, the aspect of the inter-inclusion of the inanimate, vegetative, animate, and human—
that in each of these four types, the other three types are also included in concealment—
this concealment belongs to the aspect of the essential concealment
[of the aspect of Akudim and higher,
which is above the matter of division].
And based on this, what is explained in the maamar is understood
(regarding the matter of the thirty vessels of Atzilus becoming Nefesh, Ruach, Neshama for Beriah, Yetzirah, Asiyah)
that in each of the three worlds of Beriah, Yetzirah, Asiyah there are all three categories of Chabad, Chagat, Nehi,
for the inter-inclusion of the aspects of Chagat and Nehi in Beriah,
and likewise Chabad and Nehi in Yetzirah,
Chabad and Chagat in Asiyah,
is from the aspect of concealment that is in Beriah, Yetzirah, Asiyah,
which relates to the aspect of the essential concealment
(in the analogy of the inter-inclusion of the inanimate, vegetative, animate, and human,
as above).

sections.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains that the true essence of limitation is specifically from the aspect of inter-inclusion, and therefore the question of how a limited being can come into existence from the unlimited Ein Sof arises specifically after the thirty vessels become souls for Beriah, Yetzirah, Asiyah, and the answer is that this is from the Essence of Ein Sof, which is equally present below as above.

translations.translation: And based on this, it will also be understood that after he explains the matter of the thirty vessels of Atzilus becoming Nefesh, Ruach, Neshama for Beriah, Yetzirah, Asiyah,
and the matter of the inter-inclusion in Beriah, Yetzirah, Asiyah,
the maamar asks:
"But now it must be understood how it is possible for a limited being to come into existence from the light of Ein Sof, which is unlimited."
For ostensibly, this question also applies regarding Atzilus,
since even Atzilus is a limitation,
and also regarding Beriah, Yetzirah, Asiyah,
the question ostensibly is from the very essence of the matter of limitation in Beriah, Yetzirah, Asiyah,
and not from the matter of inter-inclusion, etc.,
so why does it write "now it must be understood," etc.?
But the matter is,
that the true essence of limitation is specifically from the matter of inter-inclusion.
For in Atzilus,
since the ten Sefiros are divided from one another,
the limitation of Atzilus is an aspect of revelation
(and is not the true essence of limitation),
but when the thirty vessels of Atzilus become Nefesh, Ruach, Neshama for Beriah, Yetzirah, Asiyah,
where in each world all ten Sefiros are drawn in a manner of concealment as above,
this is the true essence of limitation.
Therefore it asks: "Now it must be understood how it is possible for a limited being to come into existence from the light of Ein Sof, which is unlimited."
And to this it answers,
that this is from the aspect of the Essence of Ein Sof, which is found below just as above, equally,
that is, specifically in the limitation of Beriah, Yetzirah, Asiyah,
the aspect of concealment that is below the aspect of revelation,
the essential concealment, which is above the definitions of concealment and revelation, is expressed.
And as is known,
that "there is a created being" is an aspect of true existence.
And this is also what the maamar concludes
regarding the matter of "I dwell in the high and holy place, and with the contrite and lowly of spirit" specifically.
And afterwards it explains that the limitation and concealment below,
which is in the aspect of the absence of division,
is analogous to the aspect of Akudim in a single vessel,
the aspect of the all-encompassing Makif that is above division.

sections.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains that the matter of engaging in Torah for its own sake draws the aspect of the essential concealment, in which all are equal, and the differences are only in the aspect of revelation, as explained in Torah Ohr.

translations.translation: And with this it will also be understood what they said, "All who engage in Torah for its own sake," etc.,
for ostensibly, engaging in Torah for its own sake is a lofty level,
and Torah speaks to the majority,
so how can the matter of engaging in Torah for its own sake apply to those who are on a low level?
But the matter is,
that since engaging in Torah for its own sake is a matter of drawing down the aspect of the essential concealment,
in this all are equal,
even though there are differences in the matter of revelation.
And analogous to what is explained in Torah Ohr,
that there is one for whom it is sufficient to [study] once in the morning and once in the evening,
and there is one who needs to fulfill "and you shall meditate in it day and night" literally,
that the difference is only in the matter of revelation, etc.
And even as the conclusion in Torah Ohr there, in the explanation of the maamar "The King's decree," that ultimately it is also drawn in revelation
(as in the aforementioned blessing)
that "the Holy One, blessed be He, will complete for him," etc.
